text: But I think, for this purpose of remembering the contribution of SIM University, I seek everyone's understanding and support that we would like to keep “新跃” in the Chinese name of SUSS.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The degree certifications can be re-issued in SUSS's name.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There is no condition that you must take an extra module.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The other uniqueness of SUSS is that it will focus on applied learning.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As pointed out by Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef and Mr Saktiandi Supaat, SUSS will retain and develop its existing strong culture in service learning, including local and overseas experiential learning, as well as project work.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These are very important aspects of applied learning.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Another important aspect is collaboration with industries and employers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: SUSS already partners the Ong Teng Cheong Labour Leadership Institute (OTCI) to deliver various programmes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am glad Mr Saktiandi Supaat raised this.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Today, they co-deliver a Diploma in Employment Relations.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And there is a good opportunity there for SUSS to strengthen that collaboration with OTCI, as well as the National Trades Union Congress, and become an AU that contributes strongly to Singapore's unique institution of tripartism.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As suggested by Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan, it will certainly also expand its offering of professional development programmes, which are not necessarily at the degree level.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These programmes are created often in collaboration with industries and other organisations, or targeted at professional development in specific fields.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And, in time to come, if they grow it enough, perhaps they can consider forming a professional academy.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Moving forward, SUSS will continue to work closely with the relevant Government bodies and industry to develop degree programmes and modular courses that have strong industry relevance, as suggested by Mr Desmond Choo, too.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For applied learning to be effective, SUSS' faculty must have good representation of experts in their respective industries.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is a point raised by Mr Ang Hin Kee.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: SUSS' faculty today consists of a large number of associates drawn from industry, many of whom are practitioners and experts in their own fields.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: SUSS will continue to build upon its teaching staff's capabilities to ensure that its course content is industry-relevant.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, in answer to Ms Denise Phua, it cannot compete in global university rankings, which are driven very much by research.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Which is why the research today at applied universities, such as SIT and SUSS, are largely done in collaboration with, or even commissioned by, companies or Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Perhaps, this is why it raised the concern and perception that we need to safeguard the autonomy of research from policymakers, a point raised by Assoc Prof Daniel Goh.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am sure Assoc Prof Daniel Goh will also appreciate that this is not the case in research-intensive universities like NUS.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For these universities, as he pointed out, the challenge sometimes is the opposite − to ensure that research is grounded and relevant to and can positively impact our communities, society and economy as well.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That should also include empirical social science research relevant to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: MOE will work with the AUs to take steps to encourage this.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As some members may know, under the Social Science Research Council (SSRC), we take a bottom-up approach.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, SUSS, as well as other universities, are free to propose quality projects with good impact.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I hope that SUSS will submit good proposals pertinent to our society, innovative, even unprecedented, and can potentially be impactful.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As Assoc Prof Daniel Goh mentioned, we will urge universities to submit interdisciplinary, or even inter-university research proposals.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We must recognise that innovation and deep insights often occur in the intersections of disciplines.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Big universities like NUS and NTU may have less motivation and incentive to have inter-university collaboration.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But actually, small universities have a strong motivation to do so.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, today, between SMU and SUTD, there has been a lot of collaboration, and, certainly, MOE will encourage more of this.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The third unique proposition of SUSS is that it will retain its focus on lifelong learning and support the education and upgrading of adult learners.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And adult learners must mean people older than 29 years old, and all ages, in fact.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The majority of SUSS' intake, or more than three quarters, are adult learners admitted into part-time programmes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They are all working and juggling studying and working.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is important to keep this aspect of SUSS, because catering to the learning needs of adults is an entire discipline in itself and we want SUSS to be an authority in this field.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think Mr Ang Hin Kee raised this.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: To cater to the adults, SUSS has taken a holistic approach to evaluating applications, taking into account not just previous academic grades, but also career accomplishments and experience.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It adopts a unique "funnel approach", for example, allowing adult learners who may not fully meet the academic requirements, to take three or four modules first, with admission to the rest of the undergraduate programme to be decided based on the performance in these first three or four modules.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, to Mr Desmond Choo's question, there is always a place for workers and mid-career entrants at SUSS.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Also, in response to Mr Ang Hin Kee and Mr Saktiandi Supaat, entry requirements, as practised today, will not change.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef asked if students at SUSS will have access to the same scholarships, bursaries and study awards as the other AUs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Louis Ng asked whether there will be a reduction in programme fees since MOE is now providing funding.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: MOE has been providing subsidies for students pursuing part-time undergraduate degree programmes at UniSIM or SIM University since 2008, and full-time undergraduate degree programmes since 2014.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan and Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef asked about financial assistance for working adults and sought clarification on the level of subsidy for part-time versus full-time programmes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Today, the main criterion for financial assistance is gross per capita monthly income of the household, which actually is a neutral measure whether the student is a young full-timer or a working adult.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In addition to Government-supported schemes, many of the universities have their own schemes to support their students.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We understand that SUSS also has existing schemes, and MOE will be happy to work with the university to explore ways to further support working adults.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Ms Denise Phua asked whether adult learners who wish to pursue full-time studies to retool for the future can be funded for more than one qualification.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But having said that, adult learners can consider a range of other subsidised training options under SkillsFuture.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These training options can lead to statements of attainment, certificates, diplomas, graduate diplomas or specialist diplomas.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Under SkillsFuture, there is no limit to attending such programmes where the fees are subsidised.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If the training is packaged under a Professional Conversion Programme, the subsidy will be even higher.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef asked about the process by which UniSIM moved from being a private entity to being under MOE's jurisdiction and an AU.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: After a period of discussion with MOE, the formal proposal to restructure UniSIM into an AU was raised with the SIM Governing Council and UniSIM's Board of Trustees in 2016.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: All parties then agreed that the restructuring would be a positive and logical next step in the development of UniSIM.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The process for restructuring was then kickstarted following an Extraordinary General Meeting on 10 November 2016, where SIM members voted in support of the proposal.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The legal changes needed to effect this were then completed earlier this year, and this Bill represents the last step in the transformation of the university into an AU.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These will focus on areas, such as student engagement, quality of teaching, quality of student experience, employment outcomes, their know-how in lifelong learning, know-how in applied learning, the relevance and standing of social sciences as a discipline, the impact and relevance of research.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Once again, I thank Members for their support of the Bill and look forward to their continued support for SkillsFuture and lifelong learning.
